question: Which enzyme is responsible for catalyzing the conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin during blood clotting?
options: Thrombin
Prothrombin
Thromboplastin
Plasmin

question: During the light-dependent stage of photosynthesis, water molecules are split in a process called photolysis. What are the direct products of this reaction?
options: Oxygen, hydrogen ions and electrons
Carbon dioxide and water
ATP and NADPH only
Glucose and oxygen

question: A person with blood type AB negative receives a transfusion of blood type O positive. Which of the following best describes the likely outcome?
options: Agglutination will occur due to Rh factor incompatibility
No reaction will occur because O is the universal donor
Agglutination will occur due to ABO incompatibility
The transfusion will be successful because AB accepts all ABO types

question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of the loop of Henle in the nephron?
options: It creates a concentration gradient in the medulla enabling water reabsorption
It filters blood under high pressure to produce filtrate
It reabsorbs glucose and amino acids via active transport
It secretes hydrogen ions to regulate blood pH

question: Nondisjunction during meiosis II results in which of the following?
options: Two normal gametes and two abnormal gametes
Four abnormal gametes
One gamete with an extra chromosome and one missing a chromosome, plus two normal gametes
All gametes receiving an extra chromosome

question: A student measures the oxygen consumption of a germinating seed at different temperatures and finds maximum consumption at 37°C with a sharp decline at 45°C. Which explanation best accounts for the decline?
options: Enzyme denaturation reduces the rate of cellular respiration
All substrate has been consumed
The seed enters dormancy at high temperatures
Oxygen becomes less soluble and unavailable

question: Which of the following hormones directly stimulates the reabsorption of sodium ions in the distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct?
options: Aldosterone
Antidiuretic hormone
Insulin
Glucagon

question: In a population where 16% of individuals show the recessive phenotype for a trait, what is the frequency of the dominant allele according to the Hardy-Weinberg principle?
During an inflammatory response, which cells release histamine causing vasodilation and increased capillary permeability?
options: Mast cells
Neutrophils
Cytotoxic T cells
B lymphocytes

question: Which of the following correctly describes the mechanism by which action potentials are propagated along a myelinated nerve fibre?
options: Saltatory conduction where the impulse jumps between nodes of Ranvier
Continuous conduction along the entire length of the axon membrane
Passive diffusion of sodium ions along the entire fibre
The impulse travels through the myelin sheath directly

question: A heterozygous tall plant (Tt) is crossed with a dwarf plant (tt). If 240 offspring are produced, how many would be expected to be tall?
Which statement accurately describes the difference between humoral and cell-mediated immunity?
options: Humoral immunity involves antibody production by B cells while cell-mediated immunity involves T cells directly attacking infected cells
Humoral immunity involves T cells while cell-mediated immunity uses antibodies
Both types use identical mechanisms but target different pathogens
Cell-mediated immunity is faster acting than humoral immunity in all cases

question: In the cardiac cycle, which event corresponds to the closure of the atrioventricular valves producing the first heart sound?
options: The beginning of ventricular systole when ventricular pressure exceeds atrial pressure
The end of ventricular diastole
The opening of the semilunar valves
The completion of atrial systole

question: A mutation causes a change in the third base of a codon from UAU to UAC. The amino acid tyrosine is coded by both UAU and UAC. This type of mutation is best described as which of the following?
options: A silent or synonymous mutation
A missense mutation
A nonsense mutation
A frameshift mutation

question: Which of the following correctly explains why carbon monoxide poisoning is life-threatening?
options: Carbon monoxide binds irreversibly to haemoglobin at the same site as oxygen, forming carboxyhaemoglobin and reducing oxygen transport
Carbon monoxide destroys red blood cells reducing their total number
Carbon monoxide blocks oxygen from entering the alveoli
Carbon monoxide reacts with plasma proteins preventing oxygen dissolution
